rules.rationale: Chalcogenide anions raised refractive index in dielectric source; polarizability raises phonon DOS peaks.
Post-transition main-group heavy elements raised source objective; high Z raises phonon frequencies.
Moderate concentration balances polarizability and bonding complexity.
Mid mean Z covers chalcogenides and post-transition heavy elements.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers chalcogenide and heavy-element polarity effects from dielectric refractive index; fails if phonon peaks are dominated by light-element modes.

rules.rationale: Light nonmetals lowered source objective; low Z lowers phonon frequencies.
Binary compositions have few bonding modes, reducing peak intensity.
Halides lowered source objective; weak halogen bonds give low phonon energies.
Low mean Z covers light nonmetals and binaries.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses the low-confidence halogen and quinary-seinery source relations; fails if halides and binaries actually carry high-lying peaks.

state.lesson: Across two development seeds, the polarity transfer skill led the mean AUC (70.85 vs 45.65) and matched the counter-hypothesis on final best score (89.57 vs 91.02), so the chalcogenide and heavy-element mechanism remains the best-grounded direction.
state.revision_summary: Retained the polarity transfer skill and counter-hypothesis unchanged except for fixing the conditions syntax to use objects instead of lists. The transfer skill's higher mean AUC across two seeds supports keeping it deployed; no new evidence justifies changing the mechanistic rules or parameters.
